items.t: Coca-Cola FEMSA stock gets higher Barclays target, rating unchanged
sum: Barclays raised its Coca-Cola FEMSA price target on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, while keeping an Equal-Weight rating on the bottler. The move followed the company's third-quarter results and lifted the broker's objective from 122 US dollars to 125 US dollars, according to AD HOC NEWS.

The higher valuation reference came after Coca-Cola FEMSA reported third-quarter revenue of 4.41 billion US dollars, above the 4.36 billion US dollar consensus cited in the report. Earnings per share reached 1.72 US dollars, below the 1.89 US dollar estimate. The combination helps explain why Barclays raised its target without changing its more cautious rating.

The company had released its third-quarter results on October 26. In its press release, Coca-Cola FEMSA said volume increased 5.3 percent and revenue rose 10.9 percent. Revenue growth reached 11.3 percent on a currency-neutral basis, while operating income advanced 15.4 percent, or 16.4 percent on a currency-neutral basis.

Majority net income increased 5.5 percent, and the company reported record consolidated third-quarter volume across its operating regions. CEO Ian Craig said Coca-Cola FEMSA continued to gain market share and maintain a strong competitive position in Mexico despite challenging consumer conditions.

Craig also highlighted double-digit operating-income growth in Brazil and Colombia, alongside progress in digital transformation. For investors, the figures point to resilient execution, but the earnings miss keeps margins, foreign-exchange effects and consumer demand central to the next assessment of the shares.

Barclays lifts Coca-Cola FEMSA stock target to USD 125
sum: Barclays raised its price target for Coca-Cola FEMSA on Tuesday, November 3, while keeping an Equal Weight rating on the bottler. MarketBeat reported that the brokerage lifted its objective from USD 122 to USD 125, pointing to a measured rather than bullish change in its assessment.

The company’s latest quarterly figures provide a mixed backdrop. Coca-Cola FEMSA reported quarterly earnings per share of USD 1.72, below the USD 1.89 consensus cited by MarketBeat. Revenue reached USD 4.41 billion and exceeded the USD 4.36 billion estimate.

MarketBeat said four analysts rate the stock Buy and six rate it Hold, producing a consensus Hold view and an average price target of USD 121.43. Other recent actions included a downgrade by Itau BBA to Market Perform with a USD 116 target, while JPMorgan raised its target to USD 127 and retained a Neutral rating.

The mixed analyst picture leaves the higher Barclays objective below some of the more constructive targets but above the latest consensus average cited in the report. For investors, the combination of revenue growth and an earnings miss keeps execution and margin development central to the valuation discussion.

Coca-Cola FEMSA stock: Record volume drives strong Q3 growth
sum: Coca-Cola FEMSA reported broad-based growth for the third quarter on October 26, 2026, with volume rising across all operations and consolidated revenue advancing at a double-digit rate. In its third-quarter results release, the bottler said revenue increased 10.9 percent year over year, while currency-neutral growth reached 11.3 percent.

Consolidated volume increased 5.3 percent to 1,089.8 million unit cases, marking a record third quarter for the company. Operating income grew 15.4 percent, or 16.4 percent on a currency-neutral basis. Majority net income rose 5.5 percent, as stronger operating performance was partly offset by a higher comprehensive financial result.

Coca-Cola FEMSA said its revenue performance reflected higher volume and revenue growth management initiatives. Unfavorable mix and negative currency translation effects limited the reported increase, but the underlying currency-neutral figure remained in double digits.

The company reported growth across its geographic operations. South America was a particular contributor, with volume up 6.0 percent to 448.3 million unit cases and revenue up 14.7 percent. In Mexico, management said revenue growth management helped sustain a strong competitive position despite challenging consumer conditions.

Chief Executive Officer Ian Craig said the company continued to gain market share during the quarter. He also pointed to the balance of Coca-Cola FEMSA's geographic footprint and described the performance in Brazil and Colombia as important drivers of double-digit operating-income growth in South America.

For the first nine months of 2026, volume increased 3.4 percent and revenue rose 6.2 percent. Currency-neutral revenue growth was 10.4 percent, while operating income advanced 8.0 percent, or 11.9 percent on a currency-neutral basis. Majority net income increased 2.7 percent over the period.

Coca-Cola FEMSA also paid the third installment of its ordinary dividend on October 13, 2026. The distribution was Ps. 0.241875 per share and formed part of a total cash distribution of Ps. 4,065.1 million.

Coca-Cola FEMSA stock: Third-quarter revenue rises 10.9 percent
sum: Coca-Cola FEMSA reported a record third-quarter consolidated volume on October 26, 2026, as revenue and operating income advanced at double-digit rates. In its third-quarter results release, FEMSA said volume increased 5.3 percent and revenue rose 10.9 percent. On a currency-neutral basis, revenue grew 11.3 percent.
Coca-Cola FEMSA stock traded at 103.50 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:16 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Coca-Cola FEMSA stock.

Operating income increased 15.4 percent in the quarter, while currency-neutral operating income rose 16.4 percent. Majority net income advanced 5.5 percent. Management attributed the performance to volume growth across all operations, revenue growth management and a stronger contribution from South America.

Chief Executive Officer Ian Craig said the company continued to gain market share despite challenging consumer conditions in Mexico. He also pointed to double-digit operating-income growth in Brazil and Colombia, as well as faster digital transformation. The comments frame geographic diversification and execution as the main supports for the current operating profile.

The quarterly margin development included a non-recurring element. Coca-Cola FEMSA recognized an insurance-claim benefit in Brazil, which lifted reported profitability. For investors, the reported operating-income increase therefore needs to be read alongside the underlying contribution from volume, pricing and cost management rather than treated as a pure recurring run-rate.

For the first nine months of 2026, volume increased 3.4 percent, revenue rose 6.2 percent and operating income advanced 8.0 percent. Currency-neutral revenue growth for the period was 10.4 percent, while currency-neutral operating-income growth reached 11.9 percent.

Coca-Cola FEMSA paid the third installment of its ordinary dividend on October 13, 2026. The payment was Ps. 0.241875 per share and formed part of a total cash distribution of Ps. 4,065.1 million, giving the quarter an additional shareholder-return aspect beyond the operating figures.

sum: - Coca-Cola FEMSA delivered solid Q2 results, with revenues up 4.7% and net income surging 16.9%.
- KOF offset flat Mexican sales with record volumes in Colombia, Guatemala, and Brazil, benefiting from favorable LatAm macro trends.
- Premiumization and strong energy drink growth, especially Monster in Brazil, provide upside beyond traditional soda volumes.
- At just over 15x forward earnings and a ~4% dividend yield, KOF remains an attractive growth and income story.

Fomento Economico Mexicano Q2 Earnings Call Highlights
sum: - Interested in Fomento Economico Mexicano S.A.B. de C.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

- FEMSA delivered strong Q2 results: Revenue rose 9.3% year over year, operating income increased 7.2%, and net consolidated income jumped 64.9% to MXN 9.2 billion, helped by lower foreign-exchange losses and associate contributions.

- OXXO Mexico returned to traffic growth, with same-store sales up 9.5% and traffic up 2%, although management expects post-World Cup normalization. The company is adjusting prices, product assortments and promotions to improve competitiveness while protecting margins.

- FEMSA is expanding its growth platforms: Spin's active users increased 22% as the company cautiously develops consumer lending, while Bara, OXXO Colombia and OXXO Brazil continued adding stores. FEMSA also completed a $300 million share repurchase and expects roughly MXN 41 billion in capital distributions through March 2027.

Fomento Economico Mexicano (NYSE:FMX) reported 9.3% year-over-year revenue growth in the second quarter of 2026 and said operating income increased 7.2%, supported by OXXO Mexico, international operations and restructuring initiatives. Net consolidated income rose 64.9% to MXN 9.2 billion, aided by lower foreign-exchange losses and a positive contribution from associates.

Chief Executive Officer José Antonio Fernández Garza said the company saw positive operational momentum across most of its businesses, while cautioning that World Cup-related demand benefits have ended and Mexico's consumer environment remains sluggish.

OXXO Mexico posted revenue growth of 11.8%, with same-store sales rising 9.5%. Traffic increased 2%, marking the first positive traffic result in eight quarters, while average ticket rose 7.4%. The chain added 253 net new stores during the quarter.

Coca Cola Femsa Q2 Earnings Call Highlights
sum: - Interested in Coca Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

- Coca-Cola FEMSA delivered solid Q2 growth: Volume rose 3.5% to 1.1 billion unit cases, revenue increased 4.7% to MXN 76.3 billion, and adjusted EBITDA grew 12.1% to MXN 15 billion. Lower sweetener and PET costs helped expand gross margin by 180 basis points.

- Mexico remained a pressure point but gained market share. Volume increased 1% despite excise-tax effects and weak consumer demand; management now expects full-year Mexican volume to be approximately flat and is evaluating the impact of an August price adjustment.

- South America was the main growth engine: Regional volume rose 6.9%, with especially strong performances in Colombia and Brazil, driving a 46.5% increase in division operating income. The company maintained its 2026 capital-expenditure target of 7%–7.5% of revenue and is reviewing options for shareholder returns.

Coca Cola Femsa (NYSE:KOF) reported second-quarter 2026 volume, revenue and profit growth, supported by record quarterly volumes in Brazil, Colombia and Guatemala, while Mexico continued to contend with an excise-tax increase and softer consumer demand.

Chief Executive Officer Ian Craig said consolidated volume rose 3.5% to 1.1 billion unit cases. Revenue increased 4.7% to MXN 76.3 billion, or 6.6% on a currency-neutral basis, as volume growth and revenue-management actions more than offset unfavorable product mix and currency translation effects.

Gross profit increased 8.8% to MXN 35.9 billion, with gross margin expanding 180 basis points to 47.1%. Craig attributed the improvement primarily to lower sweetener and PET costs, aided by the company's hedging strategy and the appreciation of most operating currencies against U.S. dollar-denominated input costs. Higher aluminum costs partially offset those benefits.
